body.text: In January 2024 an oder from a marginal community proposed it. The background was that far too many people were posting od into the wall at the time. The core idea: don't spread od information outward, don't let new passers-by learn about od, in order to protect the public; and have oders collectively obey this principle, so that the od situation can't spread and is digested internally by the circle — achieving harm reduction. It belongs to the conservative-control camp.
The reconstructed gist of the principles (illustrative, not the original text):
One: all parties must never pass od thought or od information to ordinary people or non-original OD audiences, and must resolutely maintain the inward non-proliferation of od information.
Two: resolve the od situation through the circle's self-control; share harm-reduction knowledge inside the circle, and never spread it openly outside the wall.
Three: protect passers-by from being induced by od information, and protect the circle from the attention of the iron fist.

At first it did stop a good many people trying to post od openly into the wall, and directly blocked a lot of transmission to the psychiatric users. The original intention was good: prevent proliferation from hurting passers-by.

Gradually, though, it deformed into a tool for the conservative-control camp to consolidate drug abuse. The conservative-control camp began to treat od non-proliferation as 'the July Third Proclamation': in order to consolidate drug abuse, dodge the regulatory iron fist, and fight the laws of reality, they protected drug abuse that dies in daylight from being discovered, so it could go on being abused with a clear conscience — not for harm reduction, not to keep newcomers out.

What the deformation looked like: a passer-by hesitates at the plateau's gate, and the harm-reduction camp pulls out the harms of dextromethorphan to try to talk him out of it, while the conservative-control camp retorts, 'why are you showing him documents about od, you're spreading od!'; and when they see a genuinely harmful designer-drug dealer running loose, the conservative-control camp behaves like they've spotted smuggled gold, quietly inviting people into their own home to enjoy it in private.

The inner contradiction: it was the order of a small group closing itself off, trying to fight a logically inevitable event — narrow isolationism. They forgot that the libertarians, those show-offs, weren't buying it. After the Christmas struggle session of 2024 the conservatives slid gradually toward liberal-conservative; in 2025 Guitar Zhang waved his hand, and non-proliferation became toilet paper. Most conservatives forgot everything in the course of enjoying themselves, leaving only a few control factions that hadn't kept up and some toilet girls, holding a kettle and not knowing what to do, patching things together in a vast palace, always complaining that the Douyin-Kuaishou show-offs were posting Gankang, and never getting another oder to answer.

Sage later pointed out: the real dilemma of OD non-proliferation doesn't lie in black-and-white knowledge. 'Antidepressants like sertraline cannot be used for od' is common sense, and telling people who don't know it is entirely agreeable — a typical case of knowledge doing harm reduction. But not all knowledge does harm reduction: the classic example is ''salt' can be used to unalive'. The dilemma lies in two-sided knowledge — knowledge that can be used for harm reduction and can also get people hurt. Spreading it may save someone, or hand over a knife; not spreading it may protect someone, or let them die of ignorance.
This is exactly where non-proliferation can't stay coherent: it tries to use one 'non-proliferation' line to cut apart a mass of double-edged knowledge. A line can't cut a double edge.

The od non-proliferation code was meant to stop od from spreading and hurting passers-by, and at the time it worked well; but in the end it was deformed into a tool for maintaining and consolidating od, and finally broken by its own logical contradiction. The Christmas struggle session was a conservative movement wrongly launched by people with private grudges against Gotō; through malicious rumour, exaggeration and wildly out-of-control means, it brought down the old order of the plateau, made harm reduction disappear, and let the libertarians develop strongly, allowing the show-offs to spread od and finally destroy non-proliferation.

The day non-proliferation became a sheet of waste paper was the beginning of the drug circle's ending. More and more people inside the wall looked at the drug circle through a freak-show lens; and harm-reduction knowledge, unable to be shared reasonably because of 'non-proliferation', pushed everything to the extreme.
We record the life of this principle: from protection, to consolidation, to waste paper. We don't judge the person who proposed it; we only record how it was killed by its own logic.
